responseCandidates.evidence: Original Hermes bytecode: service #25403 returns Axios response.data through #25404. Success continuation #25375 places that whole HTTP body in a locally constructed action.data.items slot; reducer #25344 iterates that local slot. Thus the successful HTTP body root is an array, not an object with an items field. The existing partial event-item model is retained under the array item shape.

trace.evidence: Service #25403 calls Axios GET with the events URL and config.params, then attaches fulfillment handler #25404.
Fulfillment handler reads the Axios result's data property and returns it as the HTTP body.
Calendar action thunk calls #25403 with the selected kindergarten and captured date-range query object.

Success continuation #25375 places the entire returned HTTP body into locally composed action.data.items at 994724, alongside local kindergartenId/date/timezone context (994719-994728); this does not establish a body-root items property.
SET_EVENTS branch iterates the locally composed action.data.items slot at 993583-993589; #25375 places the whole HTTP body there, so this proves an array body rather than a body-root items field.

For each HTTP HTTP body array entry (read via local action.data.items), the reducer calls convertFromToUtc with the entry and action.data.tz, then pushes the returned copy into the Redux events array.

Conversion helper Object.assigns the input entry into a new object, reads start_time/start_date/repeat_start and end_time/end_date, and rewrites date/time fields on that local copy. Other enumerable input fields are carried by the shallow copy.
Calendar EventsList selects state.events.events and supplies matching event records to its list renderer.
Rendered event item reads event.event_type, event.start_date, event.end_date, event.title, event.start_time, and event.end_time. Its row action/key path reads the event's unique_id and access.
Calendar-date marker reducer loop reads event.duration at 993743 from the converted event records; comparison/use does not establish a wire value type.
Event-list row callback passes the selected row event to setSelectedEvent and navigates to Event at 1715767-1715782.
setSelectedEvent action creator carries the supplied row event as action.data.
Reducer stores action.data as events.selectedEvent at 993578-993581; this is the same selected event originating from the list row.
SingleEventScreen selects state.events.selectedEvent and reads event properties for detail, export, and edit actions.
Detail-screen selector returns state.events.selectedEvent at 1719523-1719526.
Mapper called for acl_groups.view.map reads each displayed item.name, item.id, and item.type at 1719573-1719605.
ICS export helper consumes the selected event and reads title/description at 1719625-1719634; event values here are downstream of the selected HTTP HTTP body array entry.
Google Calendar export reads description and recurrence-related values from the selected event at 1719820-1719824.
Apple calendar-export generator reads is_recurring, repeat_end, and rrule at 1719893-1719905, then branches on null start_time/end_time at 1719907-1719914.
Outlook export reads start_time/end_time and branches on their nullness at 1720008-1720015; it reads description for export details at 1720077-1720082.
Edit form reads selectedEvent recurrence, description, and acl_groups fields at 1729198, 1729215, 1729395-1729402, 1729582, 1729606, and 1729626-1729628.
Edit-form selector returns state.events.selectedEvent at 1729674-1729677.

limitations: The HTTP body root is an array; action.data.items is a locally composed Redux-action envelope slot holding the whole body, not an HTTP-body property.
The model preserves the source-backed partial event-item view under the root array. Only client-read item properties are listed; other body fields and item properties are unknown.
All listed event property types remain unknown. Date construction, Moment formatting, comparison, and UI display do not prove source wire types or server constraints.

The reducer shallow-copies each item and rewrites date/time values using a timezone supplied from local user state. Those transformed Redux values are not new HTTP fields and do not establish a server timezone convention.

No response-origin read was established for root name, location, audience/course/child applicability, full_day, cancellation state, published state, or change_mode. Selected-event UI reads do not guarantee field presence or establish server semantics.

The one-capture root-array observation corroborates the source trace, but does not establish error-body shape or behavior for every role/server branch. No complete response schema, item requiredness, statuses, nullability, defaults, enum meanings, or date-range inclusivity is established.
